handover_note.complaint_summary: Resident in A-05-08 (tenant) reports karaoke in A-06-08 (owner, as reported, unverified) every weekend until about 2.00 a.m. Resident asks management to fine the source unit RM 1,000 immediately. No rule in the documents supports that fine: Act s70(2)(i) caps fines at RM 200, ABL-9 sets RM 50 per breach after verification, and only the management corporation can impose a fine (BL-7).

steps_suggested: SOP-1: Acknowledge the WhatsApp complaint today or by the next working day, through WhatsApp.

SOP-2: Ask the complainant for the dates and times of each occasion, how long each lasted, whether it has happened before, whether they reported it to the guardhouse, and any evidence. Record the unit as reported (A-06-08), not as a finding.

SOP-4: Ask the guard on duty to check on site during the next weekend quiet hours, and record what was heard, the date and the time. Check the management corporation records for any written approval of an event (by-law 10(3)).

SOP-5: Do not send any notice to the reported unit until a breach is verified. If verified, a written notice may cite House Rule 1 (Quiet Hours) and Third Schedule by-law 10(3) and the step required (lower the volume after 11.00 p.m.).

SOP-8: Hand over to the building manager: the fine asked for is not supported by any rule. Tell the complainant that any fine is decided only by the management corporation after verification, under additional by-law 9 and by-law 7.
SOP-7: Send the reply below, with the rule named and the facts still needed. Do not promise a fine or an outcome.
